records.title: PIL optimality when lead time and the lost-sales penalty grow together
records.statement: Moradi, Arts, and Drent ask whether PIL is asymptotically optimal when lead time and the unit lost-sales penalty increase at the same rate.
records.result: Theorem 1 states an iterated-limit guarantee: first let lead time tend to infinity, then let the penalty tend to infinity, under the paper's i.i.d. demand assumptions.
records.boundary: The order of limits is essential. This is the question stated in the 2025 working paper, not a claim about every joint-growth regime. A complete forward-citation audit is pending.

records.title: Optimality of the fixed non-stockout-probability policy
records.statement: For the classical periodic-review lost-sales model with linear holding and penalty costs and continuous demand, the paper conjectures that the FP3 policy whose target satisfies its optimality equation is optimal.
records.result: The paper derives an optimality equation, develops an FP3 policy and its approximation, and reports numerical comparisons. Its long-lead-time discussion argues that FP3 approaches a constant-order policy after assuming that the system reaches stationarity.
records.boundary: The conjecture is stronger than the long-lead-time argument. The paper states that the numerical evidence is not a formal proof of close-to-optimality.

records.title: Sharp constant in the disrupted-mode decentralization condition
records.statement: The paper asks whether the sufficient requirement lambda at least a plus 1 can be tightened to lambda at least a plus epsilon-zero for a universal positive constant. It also records a counterexample implying epsilon-zero must exceed 0.25.
records.result: The paper proves the Poisson-tail comparison needed for its decentralization criterion under the stated plus-1 condition and uses the result in a multitier inventory network with expediting and disruptions.
records.boundary: The question concerns the constant in the paper's tail comparison and the associated sufficient condition; it is not a general characterization of optimal disruption allocation.

records.title: Exact pipeline distribution under partial rejection and general compound-Poisson demand
records.statement: For a continuous-review (S − 1, S) lost-sales system with independently and identically distributed replenishment lead times, the source paper asks for the exact stationary distribution of the number of units on order under general compound-Poisson demand. Subsequent work narrows the unresolved case to partial rejection with a nongeometric demand-size distribution.
records.result: Chen, Jackson, and Muckstadt derive an exact stationary distribution for geometric demand sizes, also called stuttering Poisson demand, and show that this distribution depends on the lead-time distribution only through its mean. Kouki, Babai, Jemai, and Minner later give an exact recursive procedure for general compound-Poisson demand under complete rejection.
records.boundary: Under partial rejection, the 2019 recursion is exact for geometric demand sizes and approximate for a general demand-size distribution. The active question records only this residual exact-analysis case; it excludes complete rejection and the stuttering-Poisson model.

records.title: Logarithmic loss in the large-capacity guarantee
records.statement: Feng, Niazadeh, and Saberi ask whether the square-root logarithmic loss in their large-inventory guarantee for reusable-resource Bayesian online assortment can be removed. Aminian, Niazadeh, and Nuti subsequently state that their Bayesian online allocation policy attains 1 − sqrt(2/(pi k)) + O(1/k), matches the best explicit nonreusable bound, and solves the earlier reusable-resource open problem. The follow-up is currently a working paper, and this record does not extend its resolution claim beyond the model and reductions stated by its authors.
